properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-05: "just curious if it is a hard limit for a project to be limited to one graph_id? for instance, could a project say, could list 3 different graph_ids and be able to do reflow2 operations on whichever or multiple based on the question. this would be a different way of linking multiple graphs, which was an idea that we had discussed previously."

⭐ FIRST, THE MEASURED ANSWER, BECAUSE THIS ONE IS CHECKABLE AND WAS CHECKED. IT IS NOT A HARD LIMIT AT THE STORAGE LAYER.
  - Storage keys are `{graph_id}\x00{type}\x00{id}` (`dynograph_storage::keys`), so one store namespaces many graphs by construction.
  - `DesignGraph::with_graph_id` (graph.rs:191) IS A FIELD ASSIGNMENT — `self.graph_id = id.into()`. Rebinding a handle to another graph in the same store is FREE: no reopen, no lock churn, no cost. Its own doc comment says the intent out loud: "to host several designs in one storage instance".
  - `open_in_memory_as(graph_id)` already exists for the same reason.
So "list 3 graph_ids and operate on whichever" is architecturally CHEAP TODAY. What blocks it is the SERVER, not the store: the MCP service holds one `Arc<RwLock<DesignGraph>>` bound at launch, and no tool takes a graph argument.

⭐⭐ SECOND, AND IT IS THE PART THAT DECIDES WHETHER THIS IS "LINKING" AT ALL: EDGES STILL CANNOT CROSS GRAPH_IDS, EVEN INSIDE ONE STORE. `create_edge` (graph.rs:276) resolves BOTH endpoints through `self.get_node(kind, id)`, which is scoped to the bound `graph_id` — so an edge to a node in a sibling graph is refused as `NodeNotFound`. That refusal is deliberate and well-argued (a dangling edge "is not a judgement call the user might reasonably disagree with… it is a graph that cannot be walked"), and it applies here without having been written for this case.

SO THE HONEST FRAMING OF WHAT THIS BUYS: co-location gives CHEAP SWITCHING and ONE PLACE TO LOOK. It does NOT give cross-graph edges, so it does not by itself answer [BL-214] — the prose cross-references that `detect_gaps` and `propagate_change` cannot see. What it DOES do is make cross-graph edges a much shorter path IF they are ever wanted, because the key encoding already namespaces and the endpoint check is one scope decision rather than a storage redesign.

⭐ WHY THIS IS A GENUINELY NEW OPTION RATHER THAN A RESTATEMENT. `dec:nested-graphs` (accepted 2026-07-25) weighed exactly three: (a) one graph, zoom by level; (b) a graph per system; (c) a graph per ownership boundary, which it took. ALL THREE ASSUME ONE GRAPH PER STORE — the store/graph distinction was never in play, so "many graphs, one store, switchable" was not among the roads taken OR the roads not taken. It sits between (a) and (c): more separation than one graph, less ceremony than federation, and it costs none of the three obligations (a coordinate, an evidence roll-up, a freshness check) that the accepted rule says every seam must pay — because there is no seam, only a scope.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN. (a) LEAVE IT — one graph per store, federate across stores as `dec:nested-graphs` prescribes. Counter: that is what produced prose cross-references and three stores on one repo, and federation's costs are being paid by one person with no authority boundary to justify them. (b) SEVERAL GRAPHS IN ONE STORE, ONE BOUND AT A TIME — the cheapest real change: a graph reference selects which, edges stay within a graph, reads and writes stay scoped. Counter: it makes "which design am I writing to" a per-call question, which is `dec:how-a-session-is-pointed-at-a-design`'s hazard exactly — and getting it wrong writes to the wrong design. The refuse-when-several rule recorded there applies here unchanged. (c) SEVERAL GRAPHS, QUERIED TOGETHER — "operations on multiple based on the question", Anthony's stronger reading. Counter: EVERY read is `self.engine.scan_nodes(&self.graph_id, …)`, so this is not a parameter, it is a change to how every analysis is scoped, and the reports would need to say WHICH graph each finding came from or become unreadable. (d) SEVERAL GRAPHS AND EDGES MAY CROSS THEM — the full version, and the only one that answers [BL-214]. Counter: it reopens `create_edge`'s endpoint invariant, which currently guarantees every reader a walkable graph, and it needs an answer to what a cross-graph edge MEANS when one side is exported and the other is not.

⚠️ AND THE CONSTRAINT THAT CUTS ACROSS ALL OF THEM: `req:persistence` says "the design persists in-repo alongside the code" and `dec:repo-file-embedded` says the graph lives as a repo file. A single store holding several projects' designs lives in ONE repo or in none — so (b), (c) and (d) all need that requirement revisited rather than quietly contradicted. That is the same tension `dec:idea-one-owner-many-projects` option (d) hit, and it is the real price here, not the code.

WHAT MUST NOT BE RE-DERIVED: `with_graph_id` is free and already intended for this; `create_edge` refuses cross-scope endpoints and the refusal is deliberate; the MCP server binds one graph at launch; and `dec:nested-graphs` never considered this shape, so taking it is an addition to that decision rather than a contradiction of it.

NOT CHECKED: whether the export/import path carries `graph_id` in a way that would let one store's several graphs be exported separately — `export_graph` writes the bound graph, and `import_graph` "adopts the document's own graph_id", which suggests it would work, but nobody has tried it.
properties.name: OPEN — should a project hold SEVERAL graph_ids in one store and operate on whichever the question needs, which is a linking mechanism nested-graphs never considered?
properties.rationale:
Captured under the brainstorm skill at Anthony's request, and the mechanical half was CHECKED IN THE CODE BEFORE ANY OF IT WAS WRITTEN — deliberately, because three times earlier the same day this agent asserted a mechanism from a description and was wrong each time. The three facts that matter here (with_graph_id is a field assignment, create_edge scopes both endpoints, the server binds one handle) are cited to file and line so the next session argues from them rather than re-reading.

Recorded as its own node rather than folded into `dec:idea-one-owner-many-projects` because that node asks WHERE the boundary goes and this one asks WHAT A STORE MAY HOLD — they interact but are separately answerable, and one node holding both could only be half-answered.

The observation that `dec:nested-graphs` never considered this shape is the load-bearing part. That decision is accepted and its reasoning is sound; this is not a challenge to it but a fourth option it did not have, and saying so plainly is what stops a later reader treating this as reopening a settled question.
